resources.title: Global Ambassadors Program (GAP), Student Affairs
resources.description: The Global Ambassadors Program (GAP) is a summer peer-mentoring program designed to assist incoming undergraduate international and out-of-state students in acclimating to a new environment and making a smooth transition into university life at UC San Diego. The program pairs incoming undergraduate students with current student mentors (GAP Mentors can be international students, out of state students, or Californian students) in order to encourage cross-cultural exchange and create a positive transition and adjustment process for incoming students. GAP Mentors provide friendly support in order to engage our incoming undergraduate international and out-of-state students and help them create solid relationships within our campus community

resources.title: Cross-Cultural Center Internship Program, Campus Community Center
resources.description: Cross-Cultural Center Interns provide programs, services, and plan events for and with members of historically under-represented and underserved communities. Interns play a critical role in the development and operation of the CCC through front desk reception duties, facilities management, administrative tasks, educational bulletin boards, and the implementation of social justice focused education, workshops and programs. Interns learn job-related skills and the importance of teamwork, communication, and personality/working styles. They bring their knowledge of student passions, concerns, and issues to inform the Center's programs and services. Interns teach their peers about social justice concepts, current social issues and strategies for community-centered social change. The love, passion, and dedication that interns contribute to the Cross make it the ground-breaking place that it is. Every year different interns come with their own special set of interests and skills. By sharing it with the CCC, they are shaping what we are and imagining the possibilities of what we can be.

resources.title: MMW Serves, Eleanor Roosevelt College
resources.description: MMW Serves is an experiential program within UC San Diego's Making of the Modern World (MMW) program at Eleanor Roosevelt College. It combines a winter-quarter preparatory seminar with a Spring Break on-site experience focused on environmental engagement and community-based learning. The program includes engagement with Native American and historically marginalized communities, as well as fieldwork in and around California's national and state parks and other natural settings. Through these on-site experiences, MMW Serves fosters a deeper understanding of human and environmental landscapes and their interconnection. The AY25-26 Program took place in California's Colorado Desert region.

resources.title: Embedded Writing Mentor Program, Analytical Writing Program
resources.description: The Analytical Writing Program (AWP) at the University of California San Diego offers writing classes that fulfill the UC Entry Level Writing Requirement (ELWR). The program also administers the UC San Diego Writing Placement Process and offers a range of courses that develop students' critical thinking, reading, and writing skills. The program places Embedded Writing Mentors in AWP classes to provide students with individualized support. The writing mentors help students develop good topics, construct strong and interesting questions and claims, organize and support their arguments, and craft clear and coherent sentences and paragraphs. AWP's courses help our diverse population of students focus on improving their writing, learning, and practicing academic writing skills that will prepare them to succeed in all of the College Writing Programs and beyond. Students write regular short writing assignments that build the foundation for Summary & Synthesis and Argument essays. Students focus on revision as a process, ultimately revising their drafts multiple times in order to produce a strong portfolio at the end of the course. The Embedded Writing Mentor Program (EWMP) was created to provide students in AWP with one-on-one mentoring to help students reflect on their writing process with highly trained peers. More information can be found at https://awp.ucsd.edu/ .

resources.title: Trainee Advisory Leadership Council (TLAC)
resources.organization: UC San Diego MRSEC (Materials Research Science and Engineering Center)
resources.description: TLAC Member responsibilities vary based on assignment to a specific TLAC Division: Education & Outreach, Industry Interactions, Science Talks & Seminars, Trainee Workshop & Activities, and Website & Communication. Responsibilities include: Represent MRSEC trainees in administrative meetings with MRSEC leadership, and serve as a liaison between MRSEC trainees, faculty, advisory boards, affiliates, and wider materials science community at UC San Diego and beyond. Facilitate engagement of MRSEC trainees in education, outreach, and diversity activities, including but not limited to initiatives launched with the Fleet Science Center, UC San Diego Transfer Triton Day, Industry Interaction Day, National Transfer Student Week, San Diego Festival of Science & Engineering, and others. Plan and coordinate MRSEC trainee educational, social and team-building activities, including the monthly MRSEC Lunch & Learn Research Seminars and quarterly Idea Catalyst meetings. Identify MRSEC trainee speakers and presenters and assist with selecting faculty speakers at MRSEC-branded seminars and events. Identify and promote opportunities for trainee professional development. Assist MRSEC leadership in identifying best practices for increasing diversity and inclusion among trainees, with focus on broadening participation and recruitment of members from groups underrepresented in STEM. In collaboration with the MRSEC faculty and staff, work to develop and sustain a welcoming and inclusive Center environment.

resources.title: Biomedical Engineering Society UCSD Chapter
resources.description: The BMES chapter at UCSD is a student focused organization that provides both career development opportunities and events as well as social activities and a mentorship program for all UCSD undergraduate students with an interest in bioengineering and bioengineering related fields. Anyone who falls in that category is welcome to get involved! The best way to learn about what is happening is to follow us on Instagram and sign up for our mailing list which can be found in our linktree along with the latest forms and links. Our committees are the best way to get involved and connect with other students. The event pages linked above can provide an overview of what we've done, or you can contact a committee directly to hear more about their event or what they do! At the end of each year, UCSD BMES compiles a Chapter Development Report (CDR), which we send to the National BMES Organization. Based on the CDR's from over 145 student chapters, National BMES selects one chapter to be awarded the Outstanding chapter award. We received the honor of Outstanding Chapter three times out of the past 5 years, for the 2016-2017 report, 2019-2020 report, and 2021-2022 report. resources.title: HPC Student - Student Cluster Competition Team Member
resources.description: SDSC supports the Student Cluster Competition (SCC) activity, which is held at the annual Supercomputing meeting. The SCC was developed in 2007 to immerse undergraduate and high school students in high performance computing. The SCC teams consist of a mentor plus 6 students who will design and build a small cluster with support from mentors and hardware and software vendor partners. Students learn to run designated scientific applications and apply optimization techniques for their chosen architectures. SCC teams compete against teams from around the world, in a non-stop 48-hour challenge to complete a real-world scientific workload, while keeping the cluster up and running, and demonstrating to the judges their HPC skills and knowledge. Acceptance to the SC competition is competitive and requires intense preparation and skill development. San Diego Supercomputer Center (SDSC) and UC San Diego (UCSD) have sent teams to SCC since 2020, and we hope to continue the tradition.

resources.title: Visual Arts
resources.description: The Department of Visual Arts was founded in 1966 by a highly distinguished group of conceptual artists including Paul Brach, Helen and Newton Harrison and David and Eleanor Antin, who designed the MFA curriculum around theoretical and critical issues, rather than medium and technique, as was traditional at art schools. The founders were soon joined by other leading experimental artists, including Harold Cohen, Allan Kaprow, Jerome Rothenberg, Manny Farber, Standish Lawder, Patricia Paterson, Italo Scanga, Ernie Silva and J.P. Gorin. The department quickly became known as site for advanced and experimental art with a faculty who worked across disciplines and practices - the Harrisons for their engagement with environmental science, Cohen for his pioneering work on artificial intelligence, David Antin and Rothenberg for poetry as well as performance, Eleanor Antin for writing as well as photography, video and performance, Kaprow for his theory as well as his happenings, Farber for his film criticism as well as his painting, Gorin for his writing as well as his film-making. This distinguished faculty and the innovative character of the program attracted such an extraordinary applicant pool that the alumni/ae from the first five classes alone included such widely renowned artists as Allan Sekula, Martha Rosler, Yolanda Lopez and Carrie Mae Weems, as well as Fred Lonidier, Phel Steinmetz and Kim MacConnel, who were then recruited to join the faculty. Media was an area of particular strength and Babette Mangolte and Louis Hock were recruited to teach along with Gorin, Lonidier, and Steinmetz, in a program that was often ranked as the top the nation. By the early 1980s, department artists and alumni/ae had made crucial and lasting contributions to photography, video, performance, political and environmental art, computing art, art theory and criticism, the pattern and decoration movement in painting and Chicano and border art, and the post-studio, concept-based curriculum developed and shaped at UC San Diego was imitated at other institutions.

resources.title: Atmospheric River Reconnaissance
resources.organization: Center for Western Weather and Water Extremes (CW3E)
resources.description: a. Atmospheric River Reconnaissance is a Research and Operations Partnership to collect data to improve forecasts of atmospheric rivers and associated precipitation. b. "Hurricane Hunters" from the U.S. Air Force Reserve Command 53rd Weather Reconnaissance Squadron and NOAA Office of Marine and Aviation Operations fly missions above atmospheric rivers over the Pacific. c. Flights are planned by a team of meteorologists and flight directors led by CW3E personnel. d. Flight data is complemented by data from drifting buoys, profiling floats, long-duration drifting balloons, and weather stations and balloon launches on land. e. Data collected is assimilated into global forecast systems. f. Data consistently shows significant positive impact on forecasts.

resources.title: Collection Development & Management Program
resources.description: The Collection Development & Management Program (CDM) supports and advances the university?s mission of research, teaching, and public service by selecting, managing, and preserving information resources across all relevant disciplines. The program?s ultimate goal is to provide our primary user community with access to the information they need, when and where they need it, and in the form most useful to them. The program plays a critical role in supporting the cycle of knowledge through ongoing stewardship of the products of research (collections and content). We select content to purchase, using a variety of acquisition methods to maximize the reach of our funding and meet needs of users. We work with physical collections, curating the content to keep it relevant to user needs, and preserving the materials to extend its lifecycle for as long as possible.

resources.title: Marine Physical Laboratory (MPL)
resources.description: MPL was originally established as a Navy-oriented research laboratory in 1946 prior to becoming a division of Scripps Institution of Oceanography in 1949. MPL has offices both on the Scripps campus and at Navy Base Point Loma/Space and Naval Information Warfare Center (NIWC). It is the only certified facility UC-wide for classified research and holdings. Research in MPL embraces observational ocean science with emphasis on developing state of the art instrumentation for studying ocean acoustic and seismic propagation, air-sea interaction, ocean volume dynamics and ocean bottom geophysics. MPL has 31 academics in various titles (Professors, Professors in residence, Adjunct professors, Research Scientists, Project Scientists, Visiting Researchers, Specialists), 4 Research Associates/Visiting Scholars, approximately 89 staff in career, contract and limited titles, 14 postdoctoral researchers, 28 graduate students, and a large number of volunteers. MPL expends approximately $20 million annually and occupies space on- and off-campus totaling 86,800 square feet in 17 different facilities, including offices, instructional support space, and research labs.

resources.title: Geosciences Research Division (GRD)
resources.description: The Earth Section of the Scripps Institution of Oceanography encompasses research in the Cecil H. & Ida M. Green Institute of Geophysics and Planetary Physics (IGPP) and the Geosciences Research Division (GRD). Research in IGPP spans a broad range of topics in geophysics including seismology, geodynamics, geodesy and crustal deformation, geomorphology, planetary physics, geomagnetism and paleomagnetism, oceanography, and electrical methods. The Cecil and Ida Green IGPP is recognized internationally as an outstanding research and teaching institution in geophysics with a focus on maintaining modern infrastructure for conducting research including buildings, computer networks, computing mass storage, seagoing instrumentation, communications, and global observatories. Research in GRD embraces atmospheric, marine, and solid earth chemistry, cosmochemistry, paleoceanography and paleoclimate, stratigraphy, geobiology and paleoecology, hydrogeology, global and regional tectonics, and paleomagnetism.

resources.title: Seismic Design @ UCSD
resources.description: The UC San Diego Seismic Design Team provides undergraduate students with the opportunity to explore earthquake engineering through the design, build, and analysis of a 5-foot tall balsa wood model of a high-rise building. The project brings together engineering, architecture, finance and other aspects reflected in real-world projects that encourage creative thinking and facilitate learning. Every year, the team attends the Undergraduate Seismic Design Competition (SDC) hosted by the Earthquake Engineering Research Institute (EERI). The objective of the competition is to design and construct a light-weight tower that sustains minimal damage under earthquake loads, maximizes rentable floor area, and fulfills the additional guidelines provided by the EERI Student Leadership Council. These guidelines change annually based on the location of the competition in order to encourage practical and innovative ideas and to enrich the experiences of returning members.

resources.title: Theatre and Dance
resources.description: I n the 1960s, famed director Michael Langham (former head of the Guthrie Theater in Minneapolis) agreed to chair what would be a Theatre department at UCSD. At that time, a private group - the Theater and Arts Foundation - was commissioned to raise money for building a theater near the campus where Langham could launch a repertory theatre, the definitive incentive for him to settle in La Jolla. English actor and director Eric Christmas was then brought on to assist Langham for when everything was arranged. However, the money and subsequently Langham eventually fell through. Christmas stayed on, though, teaching introductory theatre courses and directing locally at the Old Globe. In 1973, UCSD finally decided to offer a major in Drama - hitherto the drama department had offered mainly introductory courses - and to pay for the construction of a theatre. Arthur Wagner was brought in in 1974 to chair the new department. Christmas would teach Acting, Floyd Gaffney was brought in to teach Dance, Stage Movement and Black Theatre, Dan Dryden would teach Technical Theatre and Design, Michael Addison taught Directing, Wagner taught Acting, Theatre History and Criticism, and Victoria Spencer served as the department's first MSO. At first a BA in Drama was offered through the school's liberal arts curriculum. A few years later, with the help of Michael Addison (who wrote the petition to the university) the graduate program was set up, offering MFAs and residencies for most of our students with La Jolla Playhouse. The department's name changed to Theatre and Dance in 1995 with the addition of the undergraduate dance studies formerly based in Physical Education led by Margaret Marshall. The evolving program offers undergraduates a Dance Major and Minor, and a Dance MFA. In 1998, UCSD Department of Theatre & Dance and UCI Department of Drama joined forces in offering a ground-breaking joint PhD in theatre history/dramatic literature that combines the faculty and resources of both campuses. Theodore and Adele Shank, with faculty and graduate students launched in 1992 the performance arts journal TheatreForum celebrating the work and published the plays of innovative theatre artists globally. TheatreForum went into hibernation in 2019 after 27 years of robust journalism. In 2019, La Jolla Playhouse began to commission the MFA graduating playwrights. Ken and Ginger Baldwin's generous philanthropy established in 1999 the Baldwin New Play Festival which showcased the MFA playwrights' work to ten professional guests nationally. The Festival - a top California venue of emerging stage talent - was renamed the Wagner Festival in 2013 when Arthur and Molli Wagner extended the Baldwin family gift for many more decades. Today, the legacy of all those who helped make the Department of Theatre & Dance what it is today lives on in the degrees offered, the facilities of Theatre District, and the various productions on stage each season. For many decades, UCSD has remained in the top rank of elite graduate theatre programs in the nation. UC San Diego Department of Theatre and Dance trains the next generation of artists and scholars who will reimagine the way we interpret our world through the performing arts. The department cultivates bold, highly talented artists capable of thriving in a variety of professional contexts. The faculty and students represent a wide range of theatrical and dance traditions and methodologies. The department encourages diversity to create work that speaks to our historical moment. The department fosters a community in which artists and scholars can realize their full potential. Production is at the core of the department's training program. It is the laboratory where the department experiments, energizes, and explores. Actors, choreographers, directors, designers, playwrights, dramaturgs and stage managers develop their skills by working on full-scale productions while being mentored by distinguished artists. The department's goal is to inspire artists and scholars with a depth of knowledge and a breadth of practice who will become leaders in the field.

resources.title: Music
resources.description: Experimentation is the DNA of UC San Diego's Department of Music. Faculty and students engage with the most vital ideas and newest technologies in order to push the boundaries of musical creation and performance, and to investigate music in the context of our time. UC San Diego's Department of Music was founded by Will Ogdon and Robert Erickson in 1966. These two innovative composers shared a belief that the most effective educational environment brings together the finest faculty with gifted students in a challenging and supportive environment that encourages each student to find her or his own path. Today, the Department of Music offers graduate degree programs in Composition, Computer Music, Integrative Studies, and Contemporary Performance, and undergraduate degrees in Interdisciplinary Computing and the Arts, Music Humanities, and Music, with an emphasis in composition, literature, performance, technology, or jazz. The Department presents close to 200 events per year in our acoustically-spectacular Conrad Prebys Concert Hall, our technologically-advanced Experimental Theater, and our intimate Recital Hall. It also maintains state-of-the-art recording and research facilities equipped with the latest audio and computer technology. Resident faculty and student ensembles include: Red Fish Blue Fish (percussion); Palimpsest and Renga (new and experimental music); Kallisti (voice and chamber opera), and Jazz, Wind, Chamber, Indian, and Gospel music ensembles. The Department's faculty have won many distinguished awards, including: Pulitzer, Guggenheim, MacArthur, and Grawemeyer awards, and awards from the American Musicological Society (Colin Slim), the Society for Ethnomusicology (Alan P. Merriam), and ASCAP (Béla Bartók and Deems Taylor). Internationally renowned artists and scholars frequently visit UC San Diego for residencies to present and record new music, to provide master classes, and to share and refine new research. These guests have included: the Arditti Quartet, Muhal Richard Abrams, Robert Ashley, Richard Barrett, Han Bennink, Lisa Bielawa, John Cage, Steve Coleman, Chaya Czernowin, Brian Ferneyhough, Paul Dresher, Steven Feld, Morton Feldman, Vinko Globokar, Lydia Goehr, Fritz Hauser, Gerry Hemingway, Toshio Hosokawa, Vijay Iyer, Helmut Lachenmann, David Lang, Anne LeBaron, Joelle Leandre, George Lewis, Lisa Lim, Alvin Lucier, Miya Masaoka, Myra Melford, Nichole Mitchell, Roscoe Mitchell, Ingrid Monson, Pauline Oliveros, Hilda Paredes, Percussion Group Cincinnati, Jean-Claude Risset, Sam Rivers, Kaija Saariaho, Jaap Schroeder, Kay Kaufman Shelemay, Wadada Leo Smith, Toru Takemitsu, John Tchicai, Chou Wen-Chung, Iannis Xenikas, and Thomas Young, among others. Graduates from UC San Diego's Department of Music have been appointed to academic positions at Oxford, Stanford, Cornell, UCLA, UCI, UCSC, New York University, American University, and other prestigious institutions in the United States, and at institutions in Australia, Brazil, Canada, China, France, Finland, Hong Kong, Korea, Iceland, Ireland, Japan, Norway, Mexico, Singapore, Spain, Taiwan and the UK. Computer music students have garnered research positions with Bose Corporation, Google and Qualcomm. And composers and performers have obtained artistic positions and premieres with the International Contemporary Ensemble, the New York Philharmonic, the Los Angeles Philharmonic, London's Philharmonia Orchestra, Iceland Symphony Orchestra, Ensemble Intercontemporain, Bang on a Can, San Francisco Contemporary Music Players, CAPUT Ensemble, Oslo Philharmonic, Either/Or Ensemble, and at festivals including Lucerne, Marlboro, Darmstadt, and Tectonics.

resources.title: Business Intelligence and People Systems
resources.description: Business & Financial Services (BFS) is the major business operation directed by the Assistant Vice Chancellor / UC San Diego Controller. The Office of the Controller provides leadership, consultation, promotion, accountability, encouragement, and expertise in building and maintaining an effective control environment. This environment is exemplified by effective business practices; well-trained and knowledgeable staff; ethical behavior, separation of duties, timely and complete communication; well-defined and understandable policy; effective risk identification and management; and quality results. Ultimately, this leads to the effective use of university resources and accurate and complete financial statements fairly reflect the results of university operations. Many programs and initiatives to ensure such an environment is in effect are developed and deployed from this office. Many of the major business processes for the campus are operated by various divisions of this department. Each division of BFS is led by a director that reports to executives within the Office of the Controller. These divisions include Financial Operations, Business Intelligence & Financial Reporting, Costing Policy & Analysis, Finance & Budget, Office of the Controller, Sponsored Projects Finance, Internal Controls & Accounting, IPPS (Disbursements & Travel, Mail Services, Logistics, Procurement & Contracts), Student Financial Solutions (Student Business Services & Central Cashiers') and Organizational Excellence. There are nearly 300 career and 100+ student employees and located in five different facilities that comprise Business & Financial Services. There are also a relatively small number of contractors and casual employees. The operations of this department encompass all campus departments and schools, but for the most part, do not include the fiscal operations of the Medical Centers, the Medical Group Clinics, or the UC San Diego Foundation.

resources.title: Stellar Evolution
resources.description: Stellar evolution is fundamental to astrophysics. UC San Diego researchers study a wide range of stars and substellar objects, from the coolest to the hottest, as well as the processes and outcomes of stellar death. Their research encompasses the formation and dynamics of stellar systems, the energetics of stellar explosions, and phenomena ranging from brown dwarfs to supernovae and kilonovae. Additionally, time-domain astrophysics plays a key role in observing and understanding transient stellar events. Understanding these stellar processes is crucial for comprehending planetary systems and is essential for exoplanet research at UC San Diego.

resources.title: MMW California Seminar
resources.description: The MMW California Seminar is an experiential program within the Making of the Modern World (MMW) Program at Eleanor Roosevelt College, UC San Diego. The program combines a special MMW course during the academic year (fulfilling MMW15 or MMW122 requirements) with a two-week on-site experience during the summer in California's San Jacinto and Sierra Nevada mountain ranges. The program includes engagement with Native American and historically marginalized communities, as well as fieldwork in and around California's national and state parks and other natural settings. Through immersive experiences, the MMW California Seminar fosters a deeper understanding of the relationship between human and environmental landscapes and their interconnection.

resources.title: Volunteer Researcher
resources.description: The Iakoucheva Lab at the Department of Psychiatry studies the molecular basis of autism using human in vitro 2D and 3D neuronal models. We are looking for a motivated undergraduate volunteer to participate in research aiming to elucidate the impact of copy number variants (CNVs) on neurodevelopmental phenotypes in autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and schizophrenia (SCZ). The research project focuses on studying cellular and molecular phenotypes implicated in ASD and SCZ such as neural population dynamics, dendritic and axonal outgrowth, synaptic impairment and network firing using CRISPR/Cas9-engineered isogenic human induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived brain cortical organoids by utilizing techniques such as single-nuclei RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq), immunohistochemistry (IHC), multi-electrode array (MEA) and PCR. What we offer: The student will be trained in basic molecular biology techniques such as cryosectioning, immunohistochemistry and analysis of microscopy images . More advanced, cutting-edge technologies, such as snRNA-seq and MEA, as well as hands-on work with iPSCs and organoids (such as generation, maintenance, sample preparation for sequencing, etc.), will depend on the student's learning aptitude and wet lab skills.

resources.title: Life Course Scholar
resources.description: The Life Course Scholars Program is housed in the Department of Urban Studies and Planning at UC San Diego. It provides an interdisciplinary, cross-generational, multi-site learning experience for UC San Diego undergraduates that will transform their understanding of aging, health, learning and research, as well as connect them more deeply to the "people and places" of surrounding San Diego communities. This unique program combines place-based, experiential, and traditional classroom-based learning methods both on and off campus. Selected students will enroll in USP 141A (Fall Quarter 2026), a "high work load - high reward" practicum-style course with a significant amount of time spent in local San Diego communities. The high expectations are reflected in the 6-unit load. The course must be taken for a letter grade. The class will meet from 9:00 a.m. - 11:50 a.m. on Wednesdays. There are a number of off-campus activities that are part of the commitment, some during regular class hours, some outside of them. Three weekend days, in particular, are required: one for a class retreat (Saturday, October 3rd, 8:45am-4pm), one for a Senior Affordable Housing Tour across San Diego (Saturday, October 24th, 8am-3pm), and one for an event we will put on at a local senior community center (Saturday, November 7th, 8am-1pm). The program is taught by Dr. Leslie R Lewis, a Senior Continuing Lecturer in the Department of Urban Studies and Planning with a background in Anthropology and Public Health.

resources.title: Neuroscience Research Opportunity for Engineering and Physics Students
resources.description: Modern neuroscience techniques have become increasingly sophisticated over the past 20 years and are now is pushing the limits of research in fields such as optics and electronics to ask new questions about brain function. Also, an increasing number of students and trainees are being trained in emerging cross-disciplinary fields such as NeuroEngineering. Our lab is focused in understanding how large collections of neurons cooperate to code for information in the brain and how these processes become altered in disease. We are looking for physics and engineering students with course work and practical experience in electronics (microcontrollers or analog electronics), optics, mechanical design, and computational techniques who are interested in developing novel approaches for studying brain function. Students interested in eventually completing their senior thesis or masters in the lab are encouraged to apply. Please send cv/resume (include major and GPA) to mshtrahman@ ucsd.edu.

resources.title: Research Assistant
resources.description: The Gustafsson Laboratory is seeking curious, highly motivated UC San Diego undergraduate students with an interest in molecular and cellular biology to join our research team. Applicants should be available to work at least 12 hours per week during the academic year. Preference will be given to students who are interested in making a long-term commitment to the laboratory. Our research focuses on understanding the pathways that regulate the life and death of cardiac muscle cells (cardiomyocytes). Mitochondrial dysfunction and activation of cell death pathways are major contributors to cardiovascular disease and heart failure. Our laboratory investigates the signaling pathways that maintain mitochondrial health and protect the heart from disease. We use a combination of genetic, molecular, and cell biology approaches, mouse models, and state-of-the-art 2D and 3D imaging techniques to study the mechanisms that regulate mitochondrial structure, function, and quality control. As an undergraduate researcher, you will receive hands-on training in modern laboratory techniques, contribute to ongoing research projects, and gradually take on increasing responsibility as you develop your research skills. This position is an excellent opportunity for students considering graduate school, medical school, or a career in biomedical research. Undergraduate researchers will assist with general laboratory operations, including maintaining laboratory supplies and organization, as well as animal husbandry for laboratory mice. Students will also perform mouse genotyping and support experiments related to cardiovascular disease research. What You'll Gain Hands-on training in modern molecular and cellular biology research techniques Experience contributing to impactful, publication-quality biomedical research Mentorship and strong preparation for graduate school, medical school, or careers in biomedical research The opportunity to earn a strong letter of recommendation based on your contributions and performance

resources.title: Artificial Intelligence and Computational Biology in Cancer and Alzheimer's Disease
resources.description: Are you a freshman interested in using artificial intelligence and computational biology to tackle some of the most important challenges in human health? Our computational biology laboratory (Ongkeko lab) brings together passionate students and scientists who use artificial intelligence, machine learning, and data-driven approaches to study cancer, Alzheimer's disease, and other dementias. Our research explores how the genome, transcriptome, and epigenome shape disease development, diagnosis, progression, and response to therapy. In cancer, we investigate tumor biology, immunology, immunotherapy, and the development of new approaches for risk prediction, early detection, and treatment. In Alzheimer's disease and dementia, we study aging, neuroinflammation, cognitive decline, and the biological mechanisms that contribute to neurodegeneration. A major focus of our laboratory is the development and application of AI-driven approaches to large-scale genomic, transcriptomic, epigenomic, clinical, and multimodal datasets to uncover patterns that may not be apparent through traditional methods. We also investigate how the microbiome and environmental factors, including microplastics, may influence cancer and neurodegenerative disease. We are seeking exceptional, intellectually curious, highly motivated, and creative freshmen who are eager to learn, collaborate, and push scientific boundaries. No prior research, programming, or computational experience is required. We will train students who demonstrate strong intellectual ability, initiative, perseverance, and a genuine desire to make meaningful contributions to science and medicine. Our students are among the most dedicated scholars on campus and typically enter the lab with an exceptional academic record, often including a GPA of 3.9 or higher and SAT scores above 1500 or ACT scores above 34. These numbers are not absolute requirements, but reflect the typical academic profile of students who have joined and thrived in our laboratory. We recognize that academic potential cannot always be captured by numbers alone and welcome applicants whose experiences, accomplishments, or intellectual potential may not be fully reflected by traditional academic metrics. In our lab, students are immersed in every stage of the scientific process-from developing hypotheses and designing studies to applying computational and AI-based methods, analyzing complex datasets, interpreting results, writing manuscripts, and contributing to scientific publications. Students become integral members of our research team and often remain with the laboratory throughout their undergraduate years before continuing to leading graduate, medical, and research programs. If you are a freshman excited by the potential of artificial intelligence and computational biology to transform our understanding of cancer, Alzheimer's disease, and human health, we encourage you to apply. Please submit a cover letter, CV, unofficial high school transcript, and SAT or ACT scores via email to rongkeko@health.ucsd.edu and wegongkeko@gmail.com . Please do not submit application materials through this portal.

resources.title: Clinical Psychology Research Assistant
resources.description: The Stress and Neuroimaging Lab at the La Jolla VA and the Neurocognition of Stress, Trauma, and Anxiety Recovery Lab at the UCSD Department of Psychiatry are looking for committed undergraduate research assistants interested in clinical psychology. The lab's studies cover a broad range of topics and generally involve functional MRI, psychiatric interviews, and a short battery of neuropsychological assessments conducted by our clinical research coordinators. The selected student research assistant would have the opportunity to assist with study tasks, such as subject recruitment, phone screening, data entry, and supporting operators during fMRI scans. Students must be willing to commit to at least 1 year of volunteering for 15 hours a week . Students who are interested in earning 199 credit are welcome to apply, but it is not required. Requirements: minimum GPA of 3.0, must be a US citizen, no criminal records. To apply, please fill out the application on our website ( https://psychiatry.ucsd.edu/research/programs-centers/snl/contact/prospective-students.html ) and send it to scancore.3@gmail.com in a PDF or Word document along with a CV/resume and unofficial transcript.

resources.title: Undergraduate Research Team: 9 Research Assistant Tracks
resources.description: The XR lab is recruiting UC San Diego undergraduate students for nine research assistant tracks beginning in late Summer 2026 and continuing throughout the 2026-27 academic year. Available research tracks Survey Scoring and Data Cleaning Behavioral and Cognitive Task Data Physiological Signal Processing and Quality Control Data Science, Statistics, and Visualization Research Software and Web Tools Literature Review, Theory, and Scientific Writing Research Documentation, Reproducibility, and Data Management Participant Recruitment, Scheduling, and Study Coordination Lab Operations, Equipment, and Condition Room Protocol Applicants may rank up to three research tracks in order of preference. Prior research experience is not required. Applicants with relevant research, technical, coding, laboratory, writing, data management, or participant facing experience may receive priority for positions that require those skills. When feasible, each track will include a paired research assistant structure in which a more experienced student and a developing researcher work together. This model is intended to distribute responsibility, support peer learning, and preserve knowledge across quarters as new students join the team. Applicants who can make a multi-quarter or full academic year commitment are strongly encouraged to apply. Students with specialized expertise may also be considered for shorter term project needs. Selected applicants may begin onboarding as early as late Summer 2026. Additional start dates will be available for Fall 2026 depending on research track needs, required training, and applicant availability. These are currently unpaid undergraduate research positions. Selected students will receive project specific training, research mentorship, regular feedback, and opportunities to develop practical skills related to their assigned research track. Application will be available until all positions are filled. Apply through the centralized application: https://forms.gle/hhtHR6pKV3D2MDst7 Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. Submission does not guarantee an interview or placement.

resources.title: Student Research Assistant.
resources.description: The Brain Mechanisms of Pain and Health Laboratory in the Department of Anesthesiology, UC San Diego under the supervision of Lab Director, Dr. Fadel Zeidan is seeking a student bolunteer will support ongoing research studies by assisting with participant recruitment, data entry, and general research administrative tasks. This role offers hands-on experience in clinical research operations within an active neuroscience and pain research laboratory. The Zeidan Laboratory investigates the neural mechanisms of mindfulness meditation and psychedelic-assisted therapy for chronic pain conditions. Our research combines neuroimaging (fMRI, ASL perfusion imaging) with randomized clinical trial designs to understand and improve treatments for pain. There are several ongoing neuroimaging focused clinical trials assessing the effects of meditation, cannabis and psychedelics on chronic pain (pediatric and adult populations) as compared to placebo. Key Responsibilities Participant Recruitment Assist with distributing recruitment materials (flyers, emails, social media postings) Screen prospective participants for study eligibility using established criteria Maintain and update recruitment tracking logs Communicate with prospective participants regarding study procedures and scheduling, under supervision Data Entry Enter and verify participant data into secure research databases (e.g., REDCap) Perform quality checks to ensure data accuracy and completeness Organize and maintain electronic and paper study files in accordance with lab protocols Research Administrative Support Assist with scheduling participant visits and coordinating calendars Help prepare study materials, questionnaires, and consent documents Support general lab organization tasks as needed Assist with IRB documentation and study binders under staff supervisionWhat You Will Gain Direct exposure to clinical research procedures and the IRB process Experience with participant recruitment strategies and data management systems Mentorship from lab faculty, postdoctoral fellows, and research staff Potential opportunities for co-authorship or acknowledgment on publications, depending on contribution and duration A letter of recommendation may be available after a satisfactory period of service (minimum [X months])

resources.title: Marketing & Growth Intern - Fashion Tech Startup
resources.description: STYLST is building the app for anyone who has stood in front of a full closet and thought, "somehow, I have nothing to wear." We're creating a smarter way to get dressed using the clothes you already own-helping women decide what to wear, what's worth buying, what to pack, and what to let go of. We're looking for curious, resourceful students who want to get in early and actually help build something. Depending on your strengths, you might work on growth experiments, social content, creator research, partnerships, customer research, or the very real behind-the-scenes work that keeps a startup moving. This is not a watch-from-the-sidelines internship. You'll work closely with a small team, own meaningful projects, bring ideas to the table, figure things out as you go, and see what it looks like to build a consumer fashion-tech company from the ground up. If you love fashion, internet culture, consumer behavior, startups-or you're just the person who always figures it out-we'd love to hear from you. Responsibilities may include: Supporting social media and content strategy across TikTok, Instagram, and other platforms Researching creators, influencers, communities, partnerships, and potential growth channels Helping with grassroots and campus marketing initiatives Supporting waitlist growth and early-user acquisition campaigns Assisting with outreach, partnerships, and marketing research Tracking trends, competitors, and emerging consumer behavior in fashion and technology Brainstorming and helping execute creative growth experiments Supporting basic marketing operations and project organization Using tools such as Canva, Google Workspace, ChatGPT, Claude, Notion, and social platforms as part of the workflow Taking ownership of projects and helping figure things out in a fast-moving startup environment We're especially interested in students who are: Resourceful and comfortable figuring things out independently Strong communicators Curious about startups, fashion, technology, consumer behavior, or social media Creative but also organized Comfortable taking initiative instead of waiting for detailed instructions Excited to learn quickly and contribute meaningfully Reliable and able to follow through on projects Prior startup experience is not required. We care more about initiative, curiosity, judgment, and willingness to learn than having the perfect resume. Schedule: Approximately 10-15 hours per week, with flexibility around school schedules. Work arrangement: Remote / flexible. STYLST is exploring internship arrangements that may qualify for academic credit depending on the student's university requirements. This is a strong opportunity for a student who wants exposure to the realities of building an early-stage consumer technology company and wants their work to have a visible impact.

resources.title: Undergraduate Research Assistant - Nano-enabled Agriculture (BS/MS Track)
resources.description: The Gonzalez-Gamboa Lab is seeking a sophomore or junior undergraduate interested in pursuing a BS/MS to join our agricultural nanotechnology research team at UC San Diego, in collaboration with the Steinmetz Lab. Our lab engineers nanoparticles derived from a plant virus as delivery vehicles for agrochemicals such as plant hormones, with the goal of helping crops survive and recover from environmental stress, including wildfire-damaged, high-salinity, and industrial runoff-impacted soils. As an undergraduate researcher, you will contribute to two interconnected lines of work: the development and characterization of virus-based nanoparticles loaded with agrochemicals, including assays to study how and when cargo is released under biologically relevant conditions, and biological validation experiments in which we grow Arabidopsis thaliana under authentic field-stressed soil conditions and track plant stress and recovery at the gene expression level. You will train and work closely with graduate students and be directly mentored by Professor González-Gamboa. We strongly prefer students who are considering graduate studies and are looking to build a sustained research experience over multiple terms. Sophomores are especially encouraged to apply.

resources.title: Undergraduate Researcher
resources.description: We are looking for a junior undergraduate to engage in a highly intensive and immersive laboratory research experience for 2 years followed by continuing on as a BS/MS student in the laboratory. This opportunity is suitable for those who are committed to eventually going to a high-level PhD program in the biological sciences and would like to be engage in state-of-the-art biological research. This opportunity is not suitable for those looking for an introductory exposure to lab research or pre-medical students seeking laboratory experience prior to applying to medical school. This is a research opportunity under the direction of a senior postdoctoral fellow. The expectation is 10-20 hours per week in the lab with BISP199 credit available and the intent to continue on into the BS/MS program for a master's degree. The project is a translational disease focused project with therapeutic implications. The lab studies how innate myeloid immunity contributes to neurodegeneration and centers on understanding neurodegenerative disease pathology and identifying novel therapeutics or gene therapy approaches as treatments. Responsibilities may include stem cell culture, stem cell differentiation, confocal imaging, molecular biology, and analysis of neuron microglia interactions. This role is ideal for a student interested in neuroimmunology, stem cell biology, and translational approaches to neurodegenerative disease.

resources.description: Drs. Walker and Tomoschuk are teaching professors in Cognitive Science with a shared interest in how people learn. Their new line of research looks at how students engage with and learn from AI-generated educational materials, and how beliefs about where those materials came from shape studying. We are looking for a detail-oriented cognitive science undergraduate to join the project at an early stage. The work involves helping build and test online experiments, proofreading study materials and questions, running participants through the Psychology SONA pool, and keeping data clean and organized. Students who stay on will have opportunities to help with analysis and with designing follow-up studies. Help build and test the online experiment (Qualtrics or similar), including checking that counterbalancing and randomization work as intended Proofread and quality-check the study materials, comprehension questions, and scoring keys Manage SONA scheduling, participant credit granting, and study records Clean and organize incoming data and flag problems early Assist with pilot testing and documenting procedures

resources.title: Lab research opportunity in transcriptomics and cellular reprogramming for undergraduates or master's students
resources.description: The Heinz lab, which studies various aspects of transcriptional regulation, has a research opportunity involving RNA-based strategies for enhanced cellular reprogramming. The ideal candidate would be a diligent undergraduate with an earnest interest in research who is planning to pursue an honors thesis or a master's degree that would allow for a multi-year commitment to the lab (preferably, a minimum of 12hr /wk). New master's students seeking to initiate a thesis project are also eligible. The applicant should have a strong background in biology-related coursework and at least some familiarity with basic lab techniques (via lab courses or prior work in a research lab). The student will work closely with a senior scientist on the project, gaining valuable research experience in and/or exposure to molecular biology (PCR, cloning, in vitro transcription), cell culture (transfection, transduction, fluorescent microscopy, flow cytometry), and high-throughput sequencing.

resources.description: The Shiley-Marcos Alzheimer's Disease Research Center (SMADRC) is in the Department of Neurosciences at the University of California, San Diego. We are part of a network of university-based sites funded by the National Institute of Health (NIH) National Institute on Aging (NIA) to collect and contribute data to the National Alzheimer's Coordinating Center (NACC) to faciliate collaborative research. The role is for a content creator specialist who has expertise with social media and other digital platforms. In particular, we would like somebody with experience creating, editing, and presenting video content and engaging digital communications about brain health, Alzheimer's research procedures, and other related topics to an audience of lay/community members. The specialist will understand how to tailor content for diverse advertising formats, including digital display, audio, social media, search, ensuring messaging aligns with channel best practices and campaign goals. The candidate's work will be displayed on our Nationally recognized Alzheimer's Disease Research Center website and social media (including YouTube) and shared with the broader National Institute on Aging community of research collaborators for modeling best practices using the ADORE portal. This position is unpaid but offers the flexibility of a completely remote role. A laptop to complete the work will be provided during the project period. If interested, contact: participate@ucsd.edu with your resume and samples of your work.

resources.title: Undergraduate Student Researcher
resources.description: We are looking for a motivated UCSD Undergraduate Student Researcher (USR) to aid experimentation and data analysis efforts on sanitization research of magnetic storage technologies ( e.g., hard disk drives, magnetic tapes, etc.). The USR will primarily perform hands-on testing and characterization of data erasure devices using a wide range of data acquisition instrumentation, and aid designing, testing, and characterizing new sanitization apparatuses. As an USR, you will develop advanced and transferable experimental research skills, contribute to active research projects, and gain awareness of the research process. This is a paid research apprenticeship opportunity, and therefore only candidates willing to commit, on average, 15-18 hours per week (in 3-4-hour work periods) should consider applying for this position; further, given the experimental nature of the anticipated research tasks, the USR will need to perform assigned work onsite. Salary rate will vary between $17.55/hour and $25.50/hour, depending on USR job duties and skills. Candidates from engineering, physics, and materials science background will be considered for this position; at the time of submission, the candidate should be at least in their Sophomore year at UCSD. Please note that this position involves access to technology that is subject to U.S. export controls. Any job offer made will be contingent upon the applicant's capacity to serve in compliance with U.S. export controls. If you would like to be considered for this position, please submit your resume and academic transcript to the principal investigator (Dr. Sergio A. Montoya; s1montoya@ucsd.edu) for consideration.

resources.description: Pre-professional internship opportunity at our brand new physical therapy clinic located in Rancho Bernardo at 16950 Via Tazon, Suite 1F. Rehabilitation interns will be directly involved in patient care by guiding patients through their exercise routines under the supervision of a licensed physical therapist. Other duties will include organizing the clinic, cleaning plinths and equipment after each use, and assisting with clerical tasks. Excellent opportunity to gain first hand experience in physical therapy profession. Perfect for pre-physical therapy students interested in attaining letters of recommendations. We have 12 full-time physical therapists,1 full-time PTA and 2 full-time occupational therapist on staff with extensive experience treating orthopedic and hand conditions. It will be a great learning opportunity for our interns especially those interested in working in healthcare setting.

resources.description: The Outpatient Rehabilitation Department at the Perlman Medical Building (adjacent to Thornton Hospital) is seeking motivated undergraduate and post-baccalaureate students interested in pursuing careers in Physical Therapy or Occupational Therapy. This internship offers a unique opportunity to gain firsthand exposure to an interdisciplinary outpatient rehabilitation setting while working alongside experienced clinicians. Our team consists of Neuro Physical Therapists, Orthopedic Physical Therapists, Occupational Therapists, and Speech Therapists who provide specialized care to a diverse patient population. resources.title: Property Management Intern
resources.description: We are looking for an intern who wants to learn through experience how homes go from construction to leased units and how to manage tenants and maintain homes for owners. Tackle the operational, financial, and legal aspects of property management. Participate in the growth of our fast-moving company Vista Nine Properties, a San Diego-based company. Learning Objectives: Leasing and Marketing - learn to use marketing strategies that attract renters, respond to inquiries, perform showings, and finalize leases. Operational Oversight - learn to use property management software Doorloop and real estate marketplace apps such as Zillow, Redfin, and Turbo Tenant Financials - gain experience in tracking Key Performance Indicators Regulatory Compliance - Understand Fair Housing regulations and local landlord-tenant laws. Intern Responsibilities: Assist with property management operations Support tenant communications, including inquiries and service requests Help coordinate maintenance and repairs with vendors Assist with property inspections and document findings Assist with lease administration and tenant onboarding Maintain and update property records and databases Support marketing efforts, including listings and social media posts Perform general administrative tasks as needed Participate in property management team meetings Contribute ideas and actions for the growth of the company. Compensation: This is an unpaid position. Minimum 4 months to 1 year committment 10-12 hours/week. Primarily remote work Flexible schedule Some work during weekends when there are showings Vista Nine Properties is a small, fast-growing property management company that self-manages multi-family properties throughout San Diego county. We work closely with AireDev, a multi-state real estate development company. We are fellow UC grads (and others) and a tech and remote-work friendly company. We are a bit nerdy, yet cool at the same time (we like to think) - think California casual but we dress up when needed. We value relationships and take hard work and self-care seriously. Please submit your resume with applicable cover letter explaining why you want to work with Vista Nine Properties and what special attributes or skills you have that you think will be a particularly positive contribution to our company. We are looking to hire immediately. You can learn more about Vista Nine at www.vistanine.com.

resources.title: Pre-professional Physical Therapy Intern
resources.description: The UCSD Pre-professional Physical Therapy Internship is a clinically-focused experience that gives the intern access to direct patient care which is an extremely valuable and rewarding experience. Located at 9400 Campus Point Dr 2nd floor, San Diego, CA 92037. The intern will also get to learn from experts in the field of Physical Therapy and Occupational Therapy. The Intern will be trained in the safe application of physical modalities such as therapeutic Ultrasound, E-stim (TENs,etc.), ice, and moist heat. The Intern will also learn anatomy and biomechanics basics in order to fulfill the internship duties. The intern will also learn how to guide a patient through an exercise program designed by the Physical Therapist safely and properly. Objectives: 1) Learn the entry level position of Physical Therapy Aide. 2) Learn what a Physical Therapist's job entails on a day to day basis. 3) Learn how to apply physical modalities and what to watch for during the use of physical modalities. 4) Learn some basic anatomy, biomechanics, and exercise techniques 5) Learn the administrative duties needed to run a Physical Therapy Clinic 6) Perform an administrative/clinical care project to enhance the quality or efficiency of the clinic.

resources.description: AI Research & Engineering Fall Internship AI Research & Engineering Intern Location: Remote (United States) Duration: Fall 2026 (Flexible) Compensation: Unpaid, academic credit may be available through participating university programs. Should they become available, applicants will automatically be considered for paid internship roles as well. About ArcellAI ArcellAI is building agentic context infrastructure for health, science, and engineering. As AI systems become more capable, organizations face a growing challenge: data is fragmented across documents, databases, applications, sensors, experiments, and operational systems. Traditional AI tools struggle because they lack the context needed to reason reliably across these environments. ArcellAI helps solve this problem by combining AI agents, multimodal data systems, provenance tracking, validation, and context-aware reasoning into a unified platform that enables trustworthy AI workflows. Our work spans healthcare, biotechnology, advanced manufacturing, engineering, and other data-intensive industries. About the Role We're looking for ambitious students who want to work on challenging AI and engineering problems in a fast-paced startup environment. As an AI Research & Engineering Intern, you will work directly with the founding team to build and evaluate AI systems, develop data infrastructure, create research prototypes, and explore emerging applications of agentic AI. This is not a typical internship. Interns are given meaningful ownership and the opportunity to contribute to real products, research initiatives, and customer-facing projects. What You'll Work On Depending on your interests and background, projects may include: - Building and evaluating AI agents for real-world workflows - Developing AI-powered applications and prototypes - Designing systems for multimodal data integration and analysis - Building tools for data lineage, validation, and reproducibility - Creating knowledge graphs and context-aware reasoning systems - Developing software infrastructure for AI and data-intensive applications - Conducting technical research on emerging AI technologies - Supporting customer pilots and product development initiatives Qualifications Required Currently pursuing a Bachelor's, Master's, or PhD degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Engineering, Mathematics, Statistics, Cognitive Science, Bioengineering, or a related field Strong analytical and problem-solving skillsExperience programming in Python or another modern programming language Ability to learn quickly and work independentlyStrong written and verbal communication skills Preferred Experience with AI, machine learning, LLMs, or data science projectsFamiliarity with Git, APIs, cloud platforms, or modern software development workflows Experience working with structured, unstructured, or multimodal dataInterest in AI agents, automation, knowledge graphs, or data infrastructure Research experience, open-source contributions, or personal technical projectsInterest in startups and emerging technologies What You'll Gain Direct mentorship from startup founders and technical leaders Hands-on experience building production-oriented AI systems Exposure to cutting-edge developments in AI, data infrastructure, and autonomous systems Ownership of meaningful projects with real-world impact Experience working in an early-stage startup environment Opportunities to collaborate across engineering, research, product, and business functions Academic Credit While this is an unpaid internship, ArcellAI has successfully worked with university internship and independent study programs, including students from UC San Diego, New York University, and MIT. We are happy to work with selected candidates and their academic departments to facilitate academic credit where available. How to Apply Please apply directly on Wellfound - https://wellfound.com/l/2CpJTv Include: Your resume A brief description of your background A short note explaining your interest in ArcellAI and this internship Applications should be submitted directly on Wellfound. Who Should Apply This role is ideal for students who: Enjoy tackling difficult technical problems Like building things from scratch Are excited by the future of AI and intelligent systems Want exposure to both research and engineering Thrive in environments with high autonomy and ownership If you've built projects, conducted research, contributed to open source, participated in hackathons, or simply enjoy learning and building, we'd encourage you to apply.

resources.title: Investigative Intern - County of San Diego Public Defender
resources.organization: County of San Diego Public Defender
resources.description: In 1988, the San Diego County Board of Supervisors voted to create an office with the mission of providing quality legal assistance to individuals charged with a crime in state court who are financially unable to retain private counsel. Thus the Office of the Public Defender was established with the mission to: "To protect the rights, liberties, and dignity of all persons in San Diego County and maintain the integrity and fairness of the American Justice System by providing the finest legal representation in the cases entrusted to us." The Department of the Public Defender has several units and divisions. The main division are ethically walled offices designed to handle the occasion when more than one person is charged with the commission of the same crime, as it would be a conflict of interest for the same office to represent all defendants charged in the case. The main divisions which have Investigative Internship opportunities are the Primary Public Defender (PPD), the Alternate Public Defender (APD), and the Multiple Conflicts Office - Major Cases (MCO). PPD handles all levels of cases and has several niche units including Juvenile Delinquency, specialty courts, and involuntary hospitalization cases. APD handles mainly adult felony cases of all levels and has a Juvenile Delinquency branch. MCO, based in downtown San Diego, handles only cases with the most serious of charges. APD and PPD maintain branch offices in downtown San Diego, El Cajon, Chula Vista, Vista, and Kearny Mesa (Juvenile Office). Investigative Interns are accepted as volunteers while enrolled in college-level coursework in Criminal Justice, Sociology, Psychology or a related field. This volunteer program provides exposure to adult and juvenile criminal cases, as well as providing practical investigation experience. Typical activities of an Investigative Intern:1. Assist attorneys and investigators with case organization and research.2. Work with investigative staff in conducting court record checks, serving subpoenas and subpoena duces tecum, obtaining school, medical or other client records.3. Assist in preparation of demonstrative evidence for presentation in court and court runs.4. May accompany investigators on field interviews and attend court hearings. Applicants must submit resume, Resume, Cover Letter, and unofficial transcript to PDI@sdcounty.ca.gov. Interviews will be held twice annually, in April/May and November.

resources.title: Research Intern
resources.description: The Ran Lab at The Scripps Research Institute is seeking one motivated undergraduate research intern to join our team. The laboratory is interested in understanding how the brain generates internal organ sensations: the mechanical stretch of the stomach signaling fullness, toxins in the gut inducing nausea and vomiting, airway irritants triggering coughing, inflammatory or damaging signals from various organs resulting in visceral pain, and how the process of interoception goes awry in diseases including hypertension, obesity, diabetes, indigestion, pulmonary diseases, eating disorders, sleep apnea, overactive bladder, and others. Here is a description of the research https://www.ran-lab.org/. An experimental research intern will participate in the project investigating the interoceptive circuitry in the brain. The intern is expected to perform the following types of experiments: mouse behavior, mouse surgery, cryo-sectioning, microscopy, histology, physiological measurements, and computational analysis. Previous undergraduate interns and research assistants of the principal investigator have received rigorous training in science, published research articles, and been admitted to the best PhD and MD-PhD programs (including Scripps, UCSD, Stanford, UCSF, Columbia, Max Planck Institute, and others).

resources.title: Online Music Merch Promotion & Infringement Prevention Assoc
resources.description: Online Music Merchandise Promotion & Infringement Prevention Associate The growth of online merchandise opportunities for rock and roll musicians has exploded. The intern will be involved in two critical aspects: merchandise promotion and infringement prevention. The first strategy will be to leverage social media advertising techniques to target potential merch customers, becoming involved in strategies to accelerate promotion of merchandising opportunities online. This will include social media platforms as well as music streaming services. The intern will become familiar with the licensing business, a massive industry becoming ever more important to musicians as other streams of revenue are diminishing in the age of music streaming. The second strategy will be the curtailing of the proliferation of counterfeit merchandise. resources.title: San Diego Opera Business Internship
resources.description: Executive Summary Provide an undergraduate business student at University of California San Diego (UCSD) the opportunity to be exposed to and learn the business aspects of a non-profit arts organization for one quarter of the school year. Scope The experience would involve circulating through the administrative departments of the San Diego Opera. The intern will provide support to each of the organizations selected, working 10 hours per week. The intern will be assigned to two or more of the following departments: Patron Services Marketing/Communication Philanthropy Financial Operations Artistic Operations and Production The intern may be involved in supporting upcoming opera productions, other performances, and annual galas. In addition, the intern will be given an introduction to the Opera administrative operations, meeting each of the Department Points of Contact, and meeting the CEO of the Opera, David Bennett. At the end of the internship, the intern will write a paper or execute a project on topic(s) of value to the San Diego Opera. For example, these topics could include a marketing plan, a fundraising plan, or inputs to the strategic plan. This would be helpful to the organization and could help the intern in their career, as they could demonstrate real-world knowledge and understanding of professional projects. The UCSD Faculty Advisor and the San Diego Opera Internship Supervisor will work with the student on the concept and provide needed information. The paper will be presented to the San Diego Opera Internship Supervisor, the San Diego Opera Department Points of Contact, others in management at the Opera, and the UCSD Faculty Advisor. The UCSD Faculty Advisor will assign a final grade for the Independent Study program.

resources.title: Business Strategy & Growth Intern - Behavioral Healthcare
resources.description: Elevé Therapy & Co is a boutique group psychotherapy practice based in San Diego, providing virtual mental health services throughout California and New York. We specialize in supporting high-achieving professionals, students, entrepreneurs, and others navigating anxiety, burnout, perfectionism, and life transitions. We are seeking a motivated Business Strategy & Growth Intern who wants hands-on experience applying business, analytical, marketing, and operational thinking within a growing healthcare organization. This internship is designed for a student interested in questions such as: How does a small healthcare business identify its strongest growth opportunities, make strategic decisions, and build the systems needed to scale sustainably? Working directly with the founder and CEO, the intern will gain behind-the-scenes exposure to entrepreneurship and small-business strategy while taking ownership of substantive projects that contribute to Elevé's continued growth. Potential projects may include: Analyzing referral sources, growth channels, and marketing performance to identify opportunities for continued growth Researching new referral ecosystems, university partnerships, professional relationships, speaking opportunities, and other potential growth channels Helping develop and maintain a CEO dashboard to organize and track key non-confidential business, growth, and marketing metrics Conducting market, industry, and competitor research and translating findings into actionable recommendations Evaluating potential new markets, services, partnerships, or business opportunities Mapping business processes and helping develop SOPs, onboarding resources, and internal systems Supporting marketing strategy and operations, including content distribution, email marketing, website initiatives, SEO-related projects, and content repurposing Researching opportunities for professional presentations, community partnerships, corporate wellness initiatives, and other visibility channels Organizing and tracking strategic initiatives to help ensure high-priority projects continue moving forward Identifying operational bottlenecks and proposing solutions to improve efficiency and scalability This is not primarily an administrative internship . The intern will be encouraged to investigate questions, analyze information, develop recommendations, and bring their own ideas and observations to weekly meetings. The intern will work directly with Elevé's founder and receive ongoing mentorship, context, and feedback. As the internship progresses, the student may take increasing ownership of projects aligned with their strengths and academic interests. Depending on the student's interests, the internship may culminate in a capstone-style project focused on an area such as growth strategy, market analysis, referral strategy, marketing performance, business operations, organizational scalability, or another mutually agreed-upon strategic initiative. This internship does not involve providing clinical services or accessing confidential client information. Interns will not have access to protected health information, billing systems, payroll, bank accounts, or other sensitive financial or clinical systems. Our goal is for the student to leave the internship with tangible projects, analyses, and recommendations they can discuss in future academic and professional settings, along with a deeper understanding of entrepreneurship, business strategy, growth, and operations within a real-world healthcare organization.

resources.title: Modeling the molecular mechanisms of aging- Research Intern
resources.description: With increased life expectancy, debilitating diseases that accompany aging are also expected to rise, including dry eye disease. Dry eye affects millions of aged adults worldwide, and tear dysfunction leads to irritation and blurred vision. The lacrimal gland (LG) is an exocrine tubuloacinar gland responsible for secreting an aqueous layer of the tear film. During the lifespan, the corneal surface and the LG are exposed to bacterial and viral infections, which may lead to a systemic disruption of the epithelial cells and induction of chronic inflammatory responses in the LG. However, the mechanism of LG aging and specific cell populations involved in this process are mostly unknown. To gain new, more specific insights into the effects of aging on different cell populations within the LG, we performed unbiased high-throughput single-cell RNA sequencing and generated the first comprehensive single cell atlases of young adult and aged LGs. In addition, using Fluorescence Activated Cell Sorting (FACS) we isolated and sequenced specific LG epithelial cell populations from young and aged mice. We discovered new unknown cell cluster markers and previously undescribed cell populations within the LGs. Our intern student will be involved in analysis RNA seq data and will help us to validate new markers/cell populations using immunohistochemistry, western blotting, qRT PCR, and some LG functional assays (secretion, proliferation, inflammatory). Each student will be given a separate project based on his/her experience and interests. Intern will participate in all lab meetings and journal clubs and can present data at the internal/external scientific meetings. Interns will be supervised by postdoctoral fellows and PI and will participate in our lab meetings and other scientific meetings (if available) ** Please note: This internship is part of the Biology Research Internship Program. Students participating in this internship are REQUIRED to obtain academic credit by enrolling in BISP 197 or AIP 197. For further information, visit aip.ucsd.edu, or contact AIP via Virtual Advising Center (VAC).
